cards.name: Terrain standing height
cards.summary: The world samples a continuous ground height from four tile corners and their centre, so units and projectiles move over a smooth surface rather than tile steps.
cards.behavior: Each map tile stores a height in elevation steps. A query converts world coordinates to a tile and a position inside it, reads the four surrounding corner heights, and averages them for a centre value. It then picks the triangle that contains the point and interpolates between the two relevant corners and the centre, producing a continuous standing height. Coordinates are clamped to the map with one tile of leeway for units entering from off-map. Movement, projectile ground checks and sensor origin heights all read this same surface.

constants.name: Elevation step
constants.unit: world units per stored height level; static conversion, no timestep

constants.name: Height level limit
constants.unit: height levels across the map range; static map format limit, no timestep

constants.name: Corner average divisor
constants.unit: corner heights averaged into the tile centre height; per height query, no timestep

cards.name: Water surface as standing floor
cards.summary: Water is a second height field that can sit above the ground, and the gameplay surface is the higher of the two.
cards.behavior: Water tiles carry their own level. When a map loads, water is placed a third of a tile below the tile ground height, so shallow water shares the walkable surface while deeper painted water can rise above it. Height queries return the maximum of ground and water, which lets hover and amphibious units cross water while ground units treat deep water as impassable elsewhere. Sensor rays test the same combined surface, so a unit can see across water it could traverse.

constants.name: Water depth below ground
constants.unit: tile fraction divisor: water sits one third of a 128-unit tile below the ground height; applied at map load, no timestep

constants.name: World coordinate shift
constants.unit: bits, converting a tile coordinate to world units (128 world units per tile); static, no timestep

cards.name: Terrain speed factor and cap
cards.summary: A droid base speed is scaled by the terrain table for its propulsion type, then clamped to that propulsion maximum and raised by experience.
cards.behavior: The speed calculation multiplies base speed by a terrain speed factor expressed as a percentage. Wheeled, tracked, legged, hover and lift propulsions each read a different column of the terrain table, so the same tile is fast for a hovercraft and slow for wheels. The result is capped at the propulsion maximum speed, then multiplied by a bonus of five percent per experience level. This final value feeds the per-update movement step, so terrain choice changes both top speed and time to cross a map.

constants.name: Percentage scale
constants.unit: divisor converting the terrain speed factor percentage into a multiplier; applied per speed recalculation, no timestep

constants.name: Hover speed on sand
constants.unit: percent of base speed; table lookup per speed recalculation, no timestep

constants.name: Experience speed bonus
constants.unit: percent of speed added per experience level; applied per speed recalculation, no timestep

cards.name: Slope and damage speed penalty
cards.summary: Pitch reduces speed linearly up to a 60-degree cutoff, heavy damage takes a third, and a floor keeps badly mapped cliffs from freezing units.
cards.behavior: The current pitch is compared against a maximum pitch of 60 degrees. Speed is multiplied by the remaining fraction, so a unit on a 30-degree slope keeps half its speed and a unit at the cutoff stops. Heavily damaged droids in single player lose one third of the remaining speed. If the result falls to 10 world units per second or below, it is raised back to 10, a guard against maps whose cliffs are not flagged as blocking. A unit that just fired a weapon without fire-on-move is set to zero instead.

constants.name: Maximum speed pitch
constants.unit: degrees of pitch at which slope speed reaches zero; checked per speed recalculation, no timestep

constants.name: Damaged speed divisor
constants.unit: divisor: heavily damaged droids keep two thirds of their speed; applied per speed recalculation, no timestep

constants.name: Speed floor
constants.unit: world units per second minimum for a moving droid; applied per speed recalculation, no timestep

cards.name: Turn and spin envelope
cards.summary: Steering blends between a slow turn rate at full speed and a fast spin rate as the droid slows, driven by propulsion stats.
cards.behavior: The direction update receives a spin angle and two rates from the propulsion stats. While the droid moves fast it turns at the lower rate; as its speed drops, the allowed rate rises toward the spin rate. The blend is linear in the absolute angle difference, capped at the spin rate, so a stationary droid can pivot quickly while a racing droid must make wide arcs. Legged propulsions expose a 45-degree spin angle with distinct spin and turn rates, which is why tracked and legged units feel different under the same steering input.

constants.name: Legged spin angle
constants.unit: degrees of angular error used to blend turn rate toward spin rate; applied per direction update, no fixed timestep

constants.name: Legged spin rate
constants.unit: engine angle units per update at standstill; propulsion stat, update-rate dependent

constants.name: Legged turn rate
constants.unit: engine angle units per update at full speed; propulsion stat, update-rate dependent

cards.name: Unit collision and slide
cards.summary: Moving droids resolve overlaps as circles in the ground plane but respect height separation, and allied soft passes halve the effective radius.
cards.behavior: The slide routine compares the mover radius with nearby droid radii. A ground unit ignores a flying unit whose height is above its own radius, and a flying unit ignores ground units below it, so aircraft pass over columns of troops. Allied units can use a soft pass that halves the combined radius, letting friendly columns squeeze past. When a droid has been frustrated by traffic for a while, friendly units are skipped entirely and it clips through them. The resolved slide vector is applied to the movement step, which keeps units on the terrain surface.

constants.name: Soft-pass radius divisor
constants.unit: divisor on the combined collision radius for allied pass-through; applied per collision resolution, no fixed timestep

cards.name: Route lanes and wall clearance
cards.summary: A* routes are widened into lanes that keep a fixed clearance from blocking terrain and bias traffic to the right.
cards.behavior: Passability is a per-tile bitfield keyed by propulsion, so wheels, tracks and hover each see a different map and lifts ignore scroll limits. After the grid search, the route is shifted into a lane: each path spine keeps a target clearance from blocking ground, offsets half the opposing separation to its right, and spreads units by an id-derived sub-lane step so a group does not stack on one line. The keep-right shift ramps in after the route starts and out before the destination so units converge on the goal instead of arriving offset.

constants.name: Wall clearance
constants.unit: world units between route spine and blocking ground; static lane geometry, no timestep

constants.name: Keep-right half separation
constants.unit: world units of lateral shift to the route right; static lane geometry, no timestep

constants.name: Sub-lane spread step
constants.unit: world units of id-hashed lateral spread; static lane geometry, no timestep

constants.name: Lane probe distance
constants.unit: tiles scanned outward when measuring wall distance; static lane geometry, no timestep

cards.name: Weapon range bands
cards.summary: Each weapon carries a short and a long range; AI range checks and target acquisition use the long band while accuracy is tuned for the short band.
cards.behavior: Weapon stats define a short range and a long range. The AI treats the long range as the engagement envelope, so a unit starts considering a target at the outer band and closes until it can fire. Range upgrades raise both bands, and the projectile helpers expose the current long, short and minimum ranges per player. Because the check is a squared distance against the long range, a target just inside the band is engaged even when the weapon accuracy is tuned for the short band.

constants.name: Long range
constants.unit: world units, outer engagement band; static stat, no timestep

constants.name: Short range
constants.unit: world units, inner accuracy band; static stat, no timestep

cards.name: Fire cadence and reload
cards.summary: Rate of fire is gated by a per-shot pause, with damage doubling the pause and reloadable weapons waiting for a reload when the magazine empties.
cards.behavior: Before firing, the code computes the earliest allowed time from the last shot plus the weapon fire pause, raised to at least one tick so a zero-pause weapon cannot fire every shot in the same tick. Heavily damaged single-player attackers double the pause. Reloadable weapons also track a magazine: when ammo reaches zero the shot waits for the reload time, and the magazine refills when that time has passed. The result is a predictable cadence that players can read from tracer spacing.

constants.name: Flak turret fire pause
constants.unit: game ticks between shots at 1000 ticks per second; static stat, no frame scaling

constants.name: Flak turret reload time
constants.unit: game ticks to reload an empty magazine at 1000 ticks per second; static stat, no frame scaling

constants.name: Flak turret magazine
constants.unit: rounds per magazine before reload; static stat, no timestep

cards.name: Projectile flight and gravity
cards.summary: Direct fire travels in a straight line at the weapon flight speed, while indirect fire follows a ballistic arc under constant gravity and aims at a target-specific height.
cards.behavior: Every projectile stores a source, a destination, the game time it was born, and a movement model. Direct projectiles advance along the source-to-destination line by flight speed times elapsed time. Indirect projectiles integrate a vertical velocity under a constant downward acceleration and a horizontal velocity, so their height traces a parabola that peaks mid-flight; the pitch is recomputed from the current vertical and horizontal speeds each update. Aiming uses a target height derived from model extents, with a fixed bonus for VTOLs, and bullets keep a small constant height above that point. A special impact-at-source flag detonates immediately, and laser-satellite shots ignore height entirely.

constants.name: Flight speed
constants.unit: world units per second along the flight path; static stat, scaled by elapsed game time

constants.name: Projectile gravity
constants.unit: world units per second squared downward acceleration; applied per flight update using elapsed game time

constants.name: Bullet flight height
constants.unit: world units above the target aim point; constant for the flight, no timestep

cards.name: Splash sphere
cards.summary: Area damage tests nearby objects in a sphere around the impact point, skipping the primary target and honouring air and ground weapon flags.
cards.behavior: On impact the radius sweep iterates every object near the impact point using the weapon radius. A target is skipped when it is the primary target, when friendly fire is disabled for the weapon and it belongs to the source player, when the weapon cannot shoot its movement tier, or when a droid position fails the sphere test. Structures are tested by their centre, droids by a sphere so aircraft can be clipped above the blast. Surviving objects take radius damage computed from the weapon splash value and effect modifiers.

constants.name: Splash radius
constants.unit: world units, sphere radius around impact; static stat, no timestep

constants.name: Splash damage
constants.unit: damage points applied to each object inside the sphere; static stat, no timestep

cards.name: Sensor range and sight rules
cards.summary: Vision is a range circle from the unit or structure, with special cases for VTOLs, unbuilt structures and anti-air sights.
cards.behavior: A viewer sensor range is read from its stats: a default sensor sees 1024 world units, a sensor tower 2048. Targets inside the circle are visible unless the tile is jammed or a wall blocks line of sight. VTOLs ignore ECM and are always visible inside range, and an anti-air structure sees VTOLs at one and a half times its range. A structure under construction sees nothing, and walls and gates have no vision. Visible targets are what weapons and the AI are allowed to engage.

constants.name: Default sensor range
constants.unit: world units radius; static stat, no timestep

constants.name: Sensor tower range
constants.unit: world units radius; static stat, no timestep

constants.name: Anti-air vision numerator
constants.unit: numerator of the 3/2 range multiplier against VTOLs; applied per visibility check, no timestep

cards.name: Terrain wavecast visibility
cards.summary: Terrain is revealed by an angular sweep that keeps a horizon height per direction, so ridges hide the ground behind them.
cards.behavior: For each sensor the code walks the tiles of a precomputed wavecast table in angular order. For every tile it computes a perspective height from the sensor eye height and the tile ground or water level, then compares it with the best height seen so far in that direction. A tile is revealed when its perspective height clears the stored horizon, and the horizon is raised to the new height, so a ridge blocks everything behind it while a valley opens a view. A leeway of 80 world units reveals ground slightly above the stored horizon, which keeps small props from punching holes in vision. The per-direction list has a fixed 1360-entry guard.

constants.name: Minimum eye height
constants.unit: world units added above a unit origin when computing its view height; applied per visibility update, no fixed timestep

constants.name: Wavecast list cap
constants.unit: entries in the per-direction horizon list; static guard, no timestep

cards.name: Structure construction
cards.summary: Buildings accumulate build points from construction droids until they reach the structure cost, with power reserved when work starts.
cards.behavior: A structure stores accumulated build points and a build rate. Each update adds the rate, which is the builder build points divided across the game updates, to the accumulated total. Starting from zero requires a power reservation for the first module; without power the contribution is zero, so a brown-out pauses construction. Completion is the accumulated points divided by the structure build points, and a module replaces the base cost with the next module cost. Demolition runs the same path with negative points.

constants.name: Bunker build points
constants.unit: build points required for the structure; static stat, consumed across updates

constants.name: Bunker build power
constants.unit: power points reserved while building; static stat, held per structure, no timestep

cards.name: Research progress and power
cards.summary: Research facilities add points toward a topic cost each update, paying its power once, and completion installs the resulting components.
cards.behavior: A lab assigned to a topic adds its research points per update, capped so it never overshoots the topic cost. The first contribution requests the topic research power; if power is unavailable the lab adds nothing. Progress is stored per player and shared across allies, so two labs on the same topic advance one bar. The interface estimates remaining time as remaining points divided by the lab point rate. When the bar fills, the research result pass unlocks the component upgrades for the player.

constants.name: Half-track propulsion research cost
constants.unit: research points accumulated at the lab point rate; static topic cost, no timestep

constants.name: Half-track propulsion research power
constants.unit: power points reserved when research starts; static topic cost, no timestep

cards.name: Target weight scoring and search
cards.summary: The AI scores candidates with weapon, distance and damage terms, searches only within sensor range plus six tiles, and switches targets only for a clearly better one.
cards.behavior: Each candidate gets a weight starting from the weapon effectiveness against the target propulsion or body class. Sensor range adds a distance bonus while actual distance subtracts thirteen points per tile, so nearer targets win. Damaged targets gain weight scaled by missing health, and target type adds a bonus: weapon and command droids outrank service units, while resource derricks outrank factories. Invisible targets and targets already under heavy fire take penalties. The search radius is the weapon long range plus any extra, clamped to sensor range plus six tiles, so a long-range weapon cannot acquire what the unit cannot see. An existing target is kept unless a new one is better by four tiles of weight.

constants.name: Distance weight
constants.unit: score points per tile of distance; applied per target evaluation, no fixed timestep

constants.name: Health weight
constants.unit: multiplier converting damage ratio percentage into score points, equal to ten tiles of distance; per evaluation, no timestep

constants.name: Target switch threshold
constants.unit: tiles of score advantage required to switch away from the current target; per evaluation, no timestep

constants.name: Search radius margin
constants.unit: tiles added to sensor range as the maximum search radius; applied per target search, no timestep
